round_interpretation: The initial actual fifteen-task comparison is complete and all 21 joint seed runs pass independent objective/allocation arithmetic verification. Only the ten-input density core and fifteen-input international-exception mask are nondominated; the latter beats the 27-input control on all three objectives in all three seeds. Literal and reduced family unions are dominated, demonstrating that component importance does not transfer automatically. U.S.-equity and international-debt within-family IC decline despite overall gains, while family NLL improves for all four. Lag improves its matched fourteen-input parent in aggregate but that branch is dominated; its usefulness on the stronger front remains unknown. This round uses both frontier branches to test rank/annual-momentum/ratio reductions, conditional lag transfer, absolute HY level and an isolated dealer-proxy bridge. No family metric or interval width is a hidden objective.
default_expected_tradeoff: Report pooled IC, Gaussian NLL and actual joint conventional Sharpe, paired seed effects, within-family forecast quality, allocation and calibrated uncertainty. Preserve genuine tradeoffs and report input savings separately.
default_falsification: A dominated result does not support the proposed simplification/transfer in this context. A pooled gain is not proof that every family improved; context conflicts and seed instability must remain explicit. Reused score dates are adaptive research, not untouched confirmation.

candidates.name: international_exception_front_without_global_rank
candidates.hypothesis: Global rank may contribute to the fifteen-input branch's density cost or weaker U.S.-equity ordering. Directly test rank in the actual shared GP rather than transferring either family's inclusion result.

candidates.name: international_exception_front_without_unskipped_annual_momentum
candidates.hypothesis: Corrected skip and intermediate momentum may suffice globally despite annual momentum's value to the separately fit debt families. A failure would establish a concrete shared exception rather than a presumed universal local basis.

candidates.name: international_exception_front_without_gold_oil_ratio
candidates.hypothesis: Oil-only may be sufficient in this compact risk/credit shared context, even though removing the ratio damaged the broad separate international-equity model. This is a new matched global context, not a claim that the earlier result was wrong.

candidates.name: international_exception_front_plus_lag
candidates.hypothesis: The newly observed lag benefit in the fourteen-input rate-exception core may transfer to the stronger fifteen-input frontier, or may again add noise under a different representation. Test all three objectives and family effects without forcing the result.

candidates.name: ten_input_density_core_plus_absolute_credit_level
candidates.hypothesis: Absolute HY level helped the compact U.S.-equity high-IC branch and may restore some lost U.S. ordering while retaining the ten-input joint core's density advantage. Its usefulness in foreign debt was different, so actual joint evidence is required.

candidates.name: ten_input_density_core_plus_dealer_proxy
candidates.hypothesis: Dealer proxy alone might capture part of the international-exception block's IC/Sharpe benefit without adding rank, trend, VIX level and the gold/oil ratio together. A successful eleven-input bridge would support a more concise shared representation; failure remains informative.
